title: Forced Oscillations
experiment: Sweeping the driving frequency ω traces the amplitude curve of Eq. 15.29, which peaks at the natural frequency ω_0. Raising the damping b lowers that peak and widens it, which is the behaviour shown in Figure 15.31.
archetype_reason: the steady-state amplitude A(ω) is a closed-form formula (Eq. 15.29), and its shape depends on m, k, b and F_0

fixed.amplitude_formula: A(ω) = F_0 / sqrt(m^2 (ω^2 - ω_0^2)^2 + b^2 ω^2), with ω_0 = sqrt(k/m)
fixed.omega_grid: ω sampled uniformly on [0.001, 3] rad/s with 3000 points, used for the peak and width metrics
fixed.width_definition: half-maximum amplitude width, following Figure 15.32; clipped to the grid ends if a crossing lies outside the grid

source.quote: Attach a mass m to a spring in a viscous fluid
where ω_0=√((k)/(m)) is the natural frequency of the mass/spring system
taking this to the limit where there is no damping (b=0) , the amplitude becomes infinite
The rotating disk provides energy to the system by the work done by the driving force (F_d=F_0sin(ωt))
The motor turns with an angular driving frequency of ω

metrics.name: amplitude
metrics.label: amplitude at ω
metrics.meaning: A from Eq. 15.29 evaluated at the current params, including the slider value of ω

metrics.name: peak_amplitude
metrics.label: peak amplitude
metrics.meaning: maximum of A(ω) from Eq. 15.29 over the fixed ω grid [0.001, 3] (3000 points), with the other params at their current values

metrics.name: width
metrics.label: half-max width Δω
metrics.meaning: on the fixed ω grid, the largest ω where A ≥ peak_amplitude/2 minus the smallest ω where A ≥ peak_amplitude/2

reproduce.claim: Driving at the natural frequency gives the maximum amplitude A_max = F_0/(bω). With m = k = F_0 = 1 and b = 0.1, this is about 10 at ω = ω_0 = 1.

source.quote: The maximum amplitude results when the frequency of the driving force equals the natural frequency of the system

contrast.claim: With four times the damping, the same oscillator has a much lower and much wider resonance peak.

source.quote: the widths of the resonance curves shown in Figure 15.31 depend on damping: the less the damping, the narrower the resonance
